title: Clicking on an action in the notification triggers the launch feedback animation
line: Clicking an action button in a notification no longer shows the app's launch feedback (busy cursor and launching task) when nothing is being started.
explanation: When an action button of a notification is clicked, libnotificationmanager asks KWin for an xdg-activation token with the sending app's id, so the app can raise a window if it wants to. KWin treats every token with an app id whose desktop file has StartupNotify as a launch and starts launch feedback (busy cursor, launching entry in the task manager), but the app is already running and often shows nothing (Thunderbird's Mark as read), so the feedback runs until it times out. The earlier MR !7052 dropped the app id, which Xaver rejected because activation needs it; he suggested a way to turn off feedback on the token instead. This adds a small KDE protocol, kde_xdg_activation_options_v1 (set_no_startup_feedback on an xdg_activation_token_v1 before commit), implements it in KWin, exposes it in KWindowSystem as KWaylandExtras::xdgActivationToken(window, appId, NoStartupFeedback), and uses it for notification actions; the token keeps its app id and serial.

commits.message:
Add kde-xdg-activation-options-v1

xdg_activation_token_v1 can't tell that a token is for a running app, so
compositors show launch feedback that never ends in a window. The new
protocol lets clients turn that feedback off for a single token.

BUG: 509169

KWaylandExtras: allow requesting a token without startup feedback

Tokens handed to apps that are already running, like the ones for
notification actions, made the compositor show launch feedback that
never ends in a window. Add the NoStartupFeedback option for them.

BUG: 509169

xdgactivation: support kde_xdg_activation_options_v1

Invoking a notification action requests a token with the app's id, so
KWin showed launch feedback although nothing was being started. Support
the new protocol so clients can turn off startup feedback for a token.

BUG: 509169

libnotificationmanager: no launch feedback for notification actions

Notification actions go to an app that is already running, but their
activation token was requested like one for a launch, so KWin showed
launch feedback. Request the token with NoStartupFeedback instead.

BUG: 509169

patches.diff:
From f0c8f6e37d17b8ae936e40f59817aa7f26e433a5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:59:34 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] Add kde-xdg-activation-options-v1

xdg_activation_token_v1 can't tell that a token is for a running app, so
compositors show launch feedback that never ends in a window. The new
protocol lets clients turn that feedback off for a single token.

BUG: 509169
---
 src/CMakeLists.txt                            |  1 +
 .../kde-xdg-activation-options-v1.xml         | 65 +++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 66 insertions(+)
 create mode 100644 src/protocols/kde-xdg-activation-options-v1.xml

diff --git a/src/CMakeLists.txt b/src/CMakeLists.txt
index 9bab6d4..b37947d 100644
--- a/src/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/src/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -17,6 +17,7 @@ install(FILES
     protocols/kde-output-order-v1.xml
     protocols/kde-primary-output-v1.xml
     protocols/kde-screen-edge-v1.xml
+    protocols/kde-xdg-activation-options-v1.xml
     protocols/keystate.xml
     protocols/org-kde-plasma-virtual-desktop.xml
     protocols/output-management.xml
diff --git a/src/protocols/kde-xdg-activation-options-v1.xml b/src/protocols/kde-xdg-activation-options-v1.xml
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..ecc1f66
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/protocols/kde-xdg-activation-options-v1.xml
@@ -0,0 +1,65 @@
+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
+<protocol name="kde_xdg_activation_options_v1">
+  <copyright><![CDATA[
+    SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Niccolò Venerandi <niccolo@venerandi.com>
+
+    SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT-CMU
+    ]]></copyright>
+
+  <interface name="kde_xdg_activation_options_v1" version="1">
+    <description summary="extra options for xdg_activation_token_v1">
+      This global lets clients set options on an xdg_activation_token_v1
+      that the xdg-activation-v1 protocol has no requests for.
+    </description>
+
+    <request name="destroy" type="destructor">
+      <description summary="destroy the global">
+        Destroying the global doesn't affect existing token options objects.
+      </description>
+    </request>
+
+    <enum name="error">
+      <entry name="already_constructed" value="0"
+             summary="the token already has a kde_xdg_activation_token_options_v1 object"/>
+      <entry name="invalid_token" value="1"
+             summary="the token isn't a valid xdg_activation_token_v1 object"/>
+    </enum>
+
+    <request name="get_token_options">
+      <description summary="get the options object of an activation token">
+        Creates a kde_xdg_activation_token_options_v1 object for the given
+        token. A token can have only one options object; requesting a second
+        one raises the already_constructed error, and passing an object the
+        compositor doesn't know as a token raises the invalid_token error.
+      </description>
+      <arg name="id" type="new_id" interface="kde_xdg_activation_token_options_v1"/>
+      <arg name="token" type="object" interface="xdg_activation_token_v1"/>
+    </request>
+  </interface>
+
+  <interface name="kde_xdg_activation_token_options_v1" version="1">
+    <description summary="options of an activation token">
+      Options set on this object apply to the token when its
+      xdg_activation_token_v1.commit request is sent; options set after the
+      commit have no effect. Destroying this object doesn't undo the options
+      already set. If the xdg_activation_token_v1 object is destroyed, this
+      object becomes inert.
+    </description>
+
+    <request name="destroy" type="destructor">
+      <description summary="destroy the options object"/>
+    </request>
+
+    <request name="set_no_startup_feedback">
+      <description summary="don't show startup feedback for this token">
+        By default the compositor may show startup feedback (such as a busy
+        cursor or a launching entry in a task manager) for a token with an
+        app_id, expecting a window of that application to show up. Clients
+        use this request when the token is handed to an application that is
+        already running and may not map or activate any window, for example
+        when a notification action is invoked. The token can still be used
+        to activate a surface as usual.
+      </description>
+    </request>
+  </interface>
+</protocol>
--
